title: Detection of intraoperative primary stability of hip endoprostheses by recording implantation-related acoustic signals
summary:
In cementless total hip arthroplasty, the femoral stem is fixed in the thigh bone without bone cement. Its initial hold is created by inserting the stem into the prepared bone with a series of hammer blows until it fits firmly. During surgery, the surgical team currently assesses this fit mainly from the resistance, visual observations, and the sound of the impacts.

Earlier studies with the Metha® short stem showed that the resulting acoustic signals change during implantation. Because these findings were obtained with only one implant system in one clinical setting, it remains unclear whether comparable changes also occur with other stem systems, different shapes of the femur, and at other study sites.

In this study, we record the sounds produced during implantation of cementless hip stems at UKGM Giessen and PIUS Hospital Oldenburg. We examine how the acoustic patterns develop during final broaching and insertion of the definitive stem, how these two stages are related, and how the patterns differ between implant systems, femoral shapes, and study sites. Available routine clinical and radiographic data up to 24 months after surgery will provide complementary information.

The study observes routine surgery and does not alter implant selection, surgical technique, or treatment. The recordings do not provide feedback during surgery and are not used to make individual decisions about primary stability.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent after provision of study information; age at least 18 years; clinical indication for primary cementless total hip arthroplasty; definitive implantation of a cementless femoral stem system covered by the effective study documents and local approvals. Treatment at an activated study site. Implant selection is based exclusively on routine clinical care and is not influenced by the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Missing written informed consent; age below 18 years; no primary total hip arthroplasty; a definitively implanted cemented femoral stem; inability to identify the definitively implanted system unambiguously; revision procedures before explicit confirmation and activation of a separate revision module; hemiarthroplasties, isolated cup revisions, and isolated head or liner exchanges. A non-evaluable audio recording excludes the participant only from the affected acoustic analysis. An indeterminate CPAH or Dorr class excludes the participant only from the respective morphology analysis. No study-specific DXA examination is required, and missing routine bone-density data are not an exclusion criterion.
